title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The pencil is extremely faint, but the layout is readable and matches the next page (p.28) almost line for line. This page is most likely show-through, an offset impression, or a first pencil draft of p.28. The legible structure is as follows.

(1) Top line: a boxed or crossed-out arithmetic line ending in an underlined result. On p.28 this is (i+p)(p+1) - (i+p-1)p = 2p+i.

(2) A ruled line, then the struck-out item E_{0S} -> E_{sigma S}.

(3) A setup diagram: S_0 -> S over k -> W, with the Frobenius lift F_S : S -> S over F_W on Spf(W) and Spec Z_p. Here S is a formal smooth W-scheme equipped with a lift of Frobenius.

(4) M = E_W, with E a free module of finite type, and F_S^*(E_S) = E_S^sigma.

(5) The Frobenius F_M : F_S^*(E_S) -> E_S, read through the identification F_S^*(E_S) = E_S^sigma, gives a map Phi : E_S^sigma -> E_S. The underlined remark says Phi induces an isomorphism after tensoring with Q_p.

(6) Boxed formulas.
- The connection matrix is A in Gamma(Omega^1_{S/W} ⊗ End(E_S)), and A' = A^sigma = F_S^*(nabla).
- Horizontality of Frobenius: Phi∘A^sigma = dPhi + A∘Phi, i.e. dPhi = Phi A^sigma - A Phi.
- Integrability: dA + [A,A] = 0, meaning dA + A∧A = 0.
- Isogeny condition: there exist Psi : E_S -> E_S^sigma and an integer i with Psi Phi = p^i id.

Purpose. This is the local-coordinate description of an F-crystal (a crystal with Frobenius isogeny) on S_0/W. It is evaluated on the Frobenius-lifted smooth lift S as a module with an integrable connection plus a horizontal Frobenius isogeny. It continues p.26, where Grothendieck computes, for the rank-2 extension category C (unit object extended by T ⊗ O_S, with Fil), how the data (Phi, omega) change under a change of splitting: Phi' = Phi + pL - F^*L and omega' = omega - dL. The conditions there are d omega = 0, F^*omega - p omega = dPhi and Phi_0 = 0. The present page generalizes this to an arbitrary free E. This is part of the 1970 work on Barsotti–Tate groups, Dieudonné crystals and filtered F-crystals (cf. the ICM 1970 talk 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux').
errors: No mathematical errors are detectable. The arithmetic (i+p)(p+1) - (i+p-1)p = 2p+i is correct, and the horizontality equation dPhi = Phi A^sigma - A Phi is consistent with the convention nabla = d + A.
Minor: '[A,A]' should be read as A∧A (or the factor 1/2 inserted, depending on the bracket convention). This is a notational issue only.

ideas.what: Local description of an F-crystal on a Frobenius-lifted smooth formal W-scheme: a free module with integrable connection A and a horizontal Frobenius Phi: E^sigma -> E, with dPhi = Phi A^sigma - A Phi
ideas.modern_name: F-crystal / F-isocrystal as a module with integrable connection and Frobenius structure (Dwork–Katz style)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dwork; Katz ('Travaux de Dwork', 1972); Berthelot; Grothendieck's crystalline program
ideas.where_published: The crystalline philosophy is in 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968) and the ICM 1970 report; the explicit matrix form is standard in Katz and Berthelot–Ogus

ideas.what: Frobenius is an isogeny: there exist Psi and i with Psi Phi = p^i id, i.e. Phi is an isomorphism after tensoring with Q_p
ideas.modern_name: F-crystal (as opposed to unit-root or F-isocrystal), Frobenius isogeny condition
ideas.where_published: Barsotti–Tate groups and crystals (ICM 1970; Montréal 1970 lectures)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a near-illegible faint duplicate or draft of p.28 and contains standard local formulas for F-crystals (connection, curvature, horizontality of Frobenius, isogeny). Nothing here is beyond what Katz, Berthelot and others published.
